title: 3rd Truth With The Verses Of Resurrection The Ease Of Resurrection By A Single Command

questions.question: What main event is described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The reviving of the earth by Allah’s creative command.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the verse about a single cry teach about resurrection?
questions.answer: It teaches that all people and jinn will be summoned and brought forward through one command.

questions.question: Which groups are specifically mentioned as being gathered in the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: Human beings, jinn, animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the verse about the Hour being like the blink of an eye show?
questions.answer: It shows that resurrection and the gathering will happen extremely quickly.

questions.question: What idea is explained by the verse stating that creation and resurrection are like one soul?
questions.answer: It means bringing all creatures into being and raising them again is as easy as giving life to one being.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s power in relation to difficulty?
questions.answer: Nothing creates any hardship for His power.

questions.question: What is meant by saying one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: Handling countless creatures at once does not divide, weaken, or delay Allah’s action.

questions.question: How does the passage connect resurrection with command rather than struggle?
questions.answer: It presents resurrection as something brought about by a single divine order, not by effort or resistance.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated stress on a single command and great ease?
questions.answer: The gathering of all creatures is fully within Allah’s control and does not become harder because of large numbers.

questions.question: What overall message does this passage give about the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: The final gathering of all beings will happen swiftly, completely, and effortlessly by Allah’s command.

questions.question: How is the bringing of the earth to life presented in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as an act done directly through Allah’s creative command.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the single cry result in?
questions.answer: It results in all being brought near and made present.

questions.question: Who are said to be brought to the plain of resurrection in that explanation?
questions.answer: All men and jinn are mentioned there.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain the speed of the Hour and the gathering?
questions.answer: It is compared to the blink of an eye, or something even faster.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention creating one being when discussing all creation and resurrection?
questions.answer: To show that for Allah, bringing back all creatures is no more difficult than bringing one to life.

questions.question: Besides humans and jinn, what other beings are included in the final gathering?
questions.answer: Animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between number and ease for Allah?
questions.answer: A greater number does not make anything harder for Him.

questions.question: What belief about divine power is reinforced by the line that one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: Allah can deal with every creature and every event at the same time without any conflict or limitation.

questions.question: How do the three verses work together in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They all support the same point that resurrection is immediate, effortless, and fully possible by divine command.

questions.question: What is the central lesson a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: The resurrection of all beings is easy and swift for Allah, no matter how vast the gathering is.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does with the earth?
questions.answer: He restores it to life.

questions.question: Through what means is this restoration said to happen?
questions.answer: Through His creative command.

questions.question: What does the passage explain about the phrase describing a single cry?
questions.answer: It explains that one command is enough to summon everyone for resurrection.

questions.question: What happens after that single cry according to the passage?
questions.answer: All are brought into the divine presence at the place of resurrection.

questions.question: What does the image of an eye blinking teach about the final resurrection?
questions.answer: It teaches that the event will occur with extraordinary speed.

questions.question: What meaning is given to the statement that creation and resurrection are like one soul?
questions.answer: The raising and gathering of all is as easy as reviving one single being.

questions.question: What broad range of creatures is included in the gathering?
questions.answer: It includes rational and non-rational creatures, as well as unseen beings and angels.

questions.question: How does the passage address the idea that many simultaneous acts might cause difficulty?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea by stating that one matter does not hinder another for Allah.

questions.question: Summarize the passage’s teaching about resurrection in one sentence.
questions.answer: Resurrection is a universal gathering accomplished instantly and easily by Allah’s single command.

questions.question: What act of Allah opens the target passage?
questions.answer: Giving life back to the earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say will bring all creatures forth for the resurrection?
questions.answer: One cry and one command.

questions.question: In the explanation of that verse, which two communities are named first?
questions.answer: Human beings and jinn.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the length of time needed for resurrection and gathering?
questions.answer: Less than or equal to the time of a blink.

questions.question: What theological point is made by comparing all people to a single soul?
questions.answer: Multiplicity does not increase difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: Which unseen beings are included alongside humans, jinn, and animals?
questions.answer: Spirit beings and angels.

questions.question: What does “great ease” add to the meaning of “single command”?
questions.answer: It shows not only that Allah can do it, but that doing so involves no burden at all.

questions.question: What kind of misunderstanding is corrected by saying one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: The mistaken idea that managing many beings at once would require divided attention or delayed action.

questions.question: How does the passage use Qur’anic verses in its teaching?
questions.answer: It uses them as direct support for the claim that universal resurrection is simple for Allah.

questions.question: What is the best statement of the passage’s overall argument?
questions.answer: Allah will gather every kind of creature for resurrection all at once, swiftly and without any difficulty.

questions.question: What change in the earth is mentioned first in the passage?
questions.answer: Its return to life.

questions.question: What does the verse about a single cry emphasize: gradual process or immediate command?
questions.answer: Immediate command.

questions.question: What is meant by being brought to the plain of resurrection?
questions.answer: Being gathered and made present for the final assembly.

questions.question: What does the comparison to the blink of an eye communicate about timing?
questions.answer: That the event will be extremely fast.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare all creation and resurrection to bringing one soul to life?
questions.answer: To teach that Allah’s power is not strained by vast numbers.

questions.question: Name the full range of beings the passage says will be brought to the Supreme Gathering.
questions.answer: Men, jinn, animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the passage say about multiple tasks in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Many tasks do not compete with or block one another.

questions.question: What can a reader infer about Allah’s command from this passage?
questions.answer: His command is fully effective and sufficient by itself to accomplish total resurrection.

questions.question: How does the passage strengthen faith in bodily resurrection and final gathering?
questions.answer: It presents scriptural evidence that the event is easy, rapid, and all-encompassing for Allah.

questions.question: What single theme ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The effortless and immediate nature of resurrection under Allah’s command.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Allah do by His creative command?
questions.answer: He revives the earth.

questions.question: What is the effect of the single cry mentioned in the first cited verse?
questions.answer: It causes all to be assembled and brought near.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to men and jinn through that one cry?
questions.answer: They will be gathered and made present at resurrection.

questions.question: What does the verse about the Hour being like a blink teach about resurrection?
questions.answer: It teaches that resurrection and the gathering after it happen with unmatched speed.

questions.question: What explanation is given for the verse comparing all creation and resurrection to one soul?
questions.answer: For Allah, creating, reviving, raising, and assembling all people is as easy as doing so for one being.

questions.question: Which classes of creatures are added beyond men and jinn when the passage expands the gathering?
questions.answer: Animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What statement in the passage directly denies any conflict between simultaneous divine actions?
questions.answer: The statement that one concern does not interfere with another.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the scale of the final gathering?
questions.answer: It portrays it as universal, including all major categories of creatures.

questions.question: What conclusion about Allah’s power is supported by all three cited verses together?
questions.answer: His power brings about total resurrection instantly and effortlessly.

questions.question: Why is this passage important for understanding the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: It explains that the event is not difficult, delayed, or partial, but complete and easy by Allah’s command.
